record_note: 199 titles from the Federal Register of Legislation: the Constitution, the Acts in force and the repealed principal Acts that have a registered compilation, each from its first version the parser can read (the Act as made, or its first compilation) through every registered compilation to the last on or before 2026-10-28 (290 compilations), and repealed Acts to their repeal; data retrieved 2026-10-28. Commits between compilations are dated by the register's version list; only compilation days are checked against official text.
verification: Verified against official text: every compilation on its compilation day (290 compilations). Changes the register dates between two compilations are credited from the endnotes, and their text on those intermediate days is not independently verified.

dates.time: 12:00 Canberra (AEST, UTC+10; AEDT, UTC+11, in daylight saving time)

scope.when_absent: this corpus records no scope notes (no commit carries Applies:); the absence is not a statement that the change reaches every case

default_reach.rule: presumption against retrospective operation; repeal or amendment does not disturb what was done or accrued before
default_reach.meaning: a Commonwealth Act is presumed not to operate retrospectively on substantive rights and liabilities unless it says so; the repeal or amendment of an Act does not affect its previous operation or any right, liability or penalty acquired or incurred under it, unless the contrary intention appears; the Constitution does not forbid retrospective laws, and the High Court has upheld a retrospective criminal law
default_reach.authority: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 (Cth) s 7(2) (effect of repeal or amendment of an Act); Maxwell v Murphy (1957) 96 CLR 261 (common-law presumption); Polyukhovich v Commonwealth (1991) 172 CLR 501 (retrospective criminal law valid); not checked in this corpus
